sources.title: Crown land use planning summary

content.value:
# Land coordination summary
Projects that may use provincially managed land should confirm land status, intended use, location, access, and overlaps with other interests early. The responsible authority determines the applicable tenure or authorization path.

sources.title: Water authorization planning summary

content.value:
# Water planning summary
Work in or near streams, wetlands, shorelines, or groundwater may require additional review. Describe the location, timing, proposed changes, and avoidance measures, then confirm current requirements with the responsible water authority.

sources.title: Provincial transportation permit planning summary

content.value:
# Transportation access summary
A new or materially changed access to a provincial transportation corridor may need review. Prepare a location plan, access purpose, traffic assumptions, drainage information, and construction details for authority confirmation.

sources.title: Permit Connect B.C. coordination summary

content.value:
# Permit coordination summary
Land-based housing, clean-power, and connectivity projects can involve more than one authority. Start with a clear project description and map, identify land and water interactions, and verify current permits through official channels.
